subject.title: [Feature]: Invoke tools directly without LLM round-trip

question: Which remaining direct-invoke surfaces should OpenClaw core support beyond the shipped HTTP/RPC/SDK and command-cron paths, and what owner/security gates are required?
rationale: The remaining scope can expose filesystem, process, session, cron, Gateway, and node actions without a model turn, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product boundary or security gate shape.

options.title: Keep umbrella and land narrow gated slices
options.body: Leave this issue open while reviewing the active host-FS and readiness PRs with explicit owner gates, safe defaults, docs, audit coverage, and live proof before merge.

options.title: Limit support to shipped paths
options.body: Declare the shipped HTTP/RPC/SDK and command-cron paths sufficient and reject host-FS, exec, slash, and CLI direct dispatch until a new maintainer-sponsored proposal exists.

options.title: Approve broader direct execution
options.body: Allow broader direct tool execution only with a named security design, upgrade proof, and operator-facing controls that make the risk explicit.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella and land narrow gated slices
recommendation.body: Leave this issue open while reviewing the active host-FS and readiness PRs with explicit owner gates, safe defaults, docs, audit coverage, and live proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The open choice centers on the dangerous-tool and owner-gated Gateway security boundary, where repository history shows related prior work.
